messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: synthetic-canary-heartbeat-us-west failed 3 times in 5m. Check: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/synthetics/canary-heartbeat?orgId=1

pagerduty: Paging on-call: ryan (team: eng-sre) — Alert: synthetic-canary-heartbeat-us-west (severity: high)

ryan: acked in PD. I'm on it. Starting with the probe logs and k8s events for monitoring/canary-probes in us-west.

ryan: quick note — last deploy to canary-probes was 02:14 UTC (image: canary-agent:v2.7.0). Could be a bad roll.

julia: pinging in — if it's a bad agent we should rollback the canary image or scale to previous replica count. I can take over if you need to hand off.

ryan: handing off to julia — i need to step into a customer call in ~8m. Julia, i left the runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/canary-probes

julia: ack. running quick checks now. kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=canary-probes -o wide

julia: found 3 pods CrashLoopBackOff across us-west-1 cluster. logs show: 
```
ERROR: failed to open tcf socket: permission denied
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "agent/main.py", line 87, in <module>
    start_probe()
OSError: [Errno 13] Permission denied
```

leo: fyi ingests show a small spike in higher latency for us-west customers ~3% of requests over the last 12m. Likely related to routing away from unhealthy hosts.

priya: customer-ops: checking support queues — 2 customers reported intermittent 503s from us-west endpoints in last 15m. severity looks low but correlated.

julia: mitigation plan: 1) scale down the failing canary replicaset to 0; 2) rollback canary-agent to v2.6.8; 3) restart proxy routing for us-west fallback policy. I'll execute steps and post commands.

julia: step1: kubectl -n monitoring scale rs/canary-agent-v2-7 --replicas=0  # scaling down broken pods

julia: step2: kubectl -n monitoring set image deploy/canary-probes canary-agent=registry.redwood/canary-agent:v2.6.8 && kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/canary-probes

julia: step3: platform-ops — can you re-evaluate the routing weight for us-west? we should shift traffic back once probes healthy.

platform-ops (ryan): got it, i'll watch the LB weights.

julia: logs after rollback show agent starting cleanly. tail of new pod: 
```
INFO: probe initialized
INFO: heartbeat ok for endpoint /healthz
```

julia: marking synthetic-check as recovered in PD. will keep an eye for 30m.

pagerduty: Incident status: acknowledged -> resolved (synthetic-canary-heartbeat-us-west). Triggered at 1779456789, resolved at 1779457105.

alyssa: thanks team. Priya — please update affected customer tickets: note that 2 customers saw intermittent 503s between ~02:12-02:30 UTC, root cause: faulty canary-agent image v2.7.0 causing probe failures -> routing fallback increased latencies. No data exfiltration.

priya: will update tickets and include timeline + workaround.

marco: assigning postmortem owner to julia. julia — please file a short incident write-up in /incidents with action items: pin canary image to stable, add preflight e2e for agent permission checks, and add alert suppression for transient rollout flaps.

julia: noted. initial postmortem draft in progress. will include commands, logs, and a proposal to gate canary image rollouts behind a small synthetic smoke test.

ryan: thanks for taking over. after my call, happy to help with the follow-up. :thumbsup:

julia: marking thread for follow-up 72h action items. closing live paging loop. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Note: automated incident timeline created: https://incidents.redwood.internal/1779456789

pagerduty: escalation logs appended to incident.

marco: adding a quick note — consider adding a permission validation in CI for the agent image so we don't push agent images that require extra capabilities without a feature flag.

julia: agreed. will add to the postmortem.

ryan: last: confirm monitoring alerts threshold tuned to avoid noisy flaps during rollouts. let's follow up in SRE retro.

alyssa: documented in the postmortem checklist. closing thread for now. :lock:
